newsitem.title: CHINA: China says committed to opening stock markets.
newsitem.headline: China says committed to opening stock markets.

text.p: China said on Thursday it was committed to market-oriented stock markets but that standardisation was a precondition for their development.

A commentary published by all major securities newspapers said Beijing believed the establishment and development of market-oriented stock markets was one of the key tasks in China's efforts to build up a market economy.
"Setting up securities markets is an important way to promote the rational allocation of resources and build up a market-oriented economic system," the commentary said.
"Consequently, the principle of actively and steadily developing the securities markets has been included in China's 1996-2000 Five-Year Plan and in the economic programme up to 2010," it said.

The comments followed up on a tough article in the People's Daily on Monday which warned that China's stock markets were overheated and that Beijing would not step in to help investors in the event of a crash.

Most shares on the Shanghai and Shenzhen exchanges hit the 10 percent limit-down level on Monday and Tuesday in response to the People's Daily article, but regained some ground on Wednesday largely on the basis of supportive official comments.
